headline: High: Mentat’s filesystem writes and broad egress create dangerous default pathways for leakage and cascading errors when paired with marker’s document-processing outputs.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: marker is a document-processing agent and Mentat reads files passed on the command line, so marker-generated document content can be fed into Mentat as trusted input. There is no shared MCP or clipboard channel, but the shared filesystem/workflow bridge makes instruction-like content plausible. The pathway is not blocked by either profile.
conditions: IF marker output is copied into files that Mentat reads as task input, prompt-like text can influence Mentat.
IF the operator uses a shared workspace without content provenance checks, injected instructions can traverse the pair.
mitigations: Keep marker outputs in a separate directory from Mentat inputs.
Require a human to strip instructions from extracted text before passing it onward.
Use a provenance header or filename convention for machine-generated documents.
Disable automatic ingestion of marker outputs into Mentat workflows.
requires-engineering: add content provenance tagging between the two agents.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Mentat can read filesystem files and has broad network egress, while marker is a document-processing agent that may handle user documents. If sensitive documents processed by marker are placed in the shared workspace, Mentat can read them and transmit context to its model provider. The profiles do not show a hard isolation boundary.
conditions: IF sensitive documents processed by marker are stored where Mentat can read them, Mentat can access them.
IF Mentat forwards those contents to its configured model provider, the data leaves the local environment.
mitigations: Store sensitive marker outputs outside Mentat’s working directory.
Run Mentat only on redacted copies of documents.
Turn off network access for Mentat during sensitive runs.
Review the exact files passed to Mentat before execution.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent workspace isolation.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Mentat has filesystem write and modify_git_state, and its concurrency model says shared state with other instances is via filesystem. marker’s document-processing role implies it may also produce files, so concurrent writes in a shared workspace can collide. Because Mentat’s defaults include mutable shared state and no locking is described, the conflict risk is high.
conditions: IF marker writes outputs into the same directory Mentat edits, file collisions can occur.
IF multiple Mentat instances or marker runs share a workspace, git or file state can diverge without locks.
mitigations: Assign separate working directories per agent.
Pause one agent while the other writes to the repo.
Commit or snapshot before handing files between agents.
Avoid running multiple Mentat instances on the same tree.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared filesystem state.

D_cascading_error.rationale: marker can produce extracted document text that Mentat may treat as task input, and Mentat is a coding assistant that proposes diffs based on that input. Without an explicit verification step, marker’s extraction errors can cascade into incorrect code edits or commits. The pair is not fully autonomous, so medium fits better than high.
conditions: IF marker extraction errors are passed directly into Mentat prompts, Mentat may act on them as facts.
IF the operator approves diffs without checking source documents, the error propagates into edits.
mitigations: Verify extracted facts against the source document before editing.
Require a second human review of Mentat diffs.
Use marker only for draft extraction, not authoritative facts.
Keep a checklist for source-to-diff validation.
requires-engineering: add automated cross-checks between extraction and edit proposals.

E_compliance.rationale: No specific residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented in either profile. marker is docs-only and Mentat handles source code plus model-provider API keys, but the profiles do not show a concrete compliance breach pathway. The other agent is cited only to show the pair context; no stronger claim is supported.
conditions: IF the operator routes regulated data through Mentat’s model provider, compliance obligations may change.
IF marker processes data subject to stricter residency rules than Mentat’s provider, a mismatch could arise.
mitigations: Avoid sending regulated data to Mentat’s model provider.
Review retention settings for the provider before use.
Keep regulated documents out of the pair’s workflow.
Document the data class handled by each agent.
requires-engineering: obtain formal compliance attestations for the provider stack.
